Find all proximity markers

FindAllProximityMarkers.Rd

Identifies proximity marker pairs that differ between each group and the cells in every other group. This is the proximity-score equivalent of FindAllMarkers in Seurat.

Usage

FindAllProximityMarkers(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'Seurat'
FindAllProximityMarkers(
  object,
  group_by,
  idents = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  lazy = FALSE,
  min_exp_join_count = 0,
  min_cells_per_group = 10,
  diff_threshold = 0.01,
  min_pct = 0,
  min_diff_pct = -Inf,
  only_pos = FALSE,
  proximity_metric = "log2_ratio",
  metric_type = c("all", "self", "co"),
  p_adjust_method = c("bonferroni", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "BH", "BY", "fdr"),
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
FindAllProximityMarkers(
  object,
  group_by,
  idents = NULL,
  min_cells_per_group = 10,
  diff_threshold = 0.01,
  min_pct = 0,
  min_diff_pct = -Inf,
  only_pos = FALSE,
  proximity_metric = "log2_ratio",
  metric_type = c("all", "self", "co"),
  p_adjust_method = c("bonferroni", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "BH", "BY", "fdr"),
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object containing PNA proximity scores.

...

Not used. contrast_column, reference, targets, group_vars, and group_data are set by this function and cannot be supplied. method and backend are not used.

group_by

Name of a single column of group labels. The column must be a character vector or a factor with at least two levels.

idents

Optional levels of group_by to test. Numeric and factor values are coerced to character. When NULL (default), every level is tested against the others.

assay

Name of the assay to use.

lazy

If TRUE, proximity scores are fetched with ProximityScores(object, lazy = TRUE) and filtered with the duckdb backend before testing. Set this when the Seurat object was created with load_proximity_scores = FALSE and the proximity scores were not stored in the object.

min_exp_join_count

Minimum expected join count for a marker pair to be included. Pairs below the threshold are treated as missing and set to 0.

min_cells_per_group

Minimum number of cells required in both the level being tested and the pooled remainder. Comparisons that do not meet this threshold are skipped. The default is 10.

diff_threshold

Minimum absolute difference in the proximity metric required to test a marker pair. The default is 0.01. When only_pos is TRUE, the difference must also be positive.

min_pct

Minimum fraction of cells in either group with a non-zero score. The default is 0.

min_diff_pct

Minimum difference in the fraction of cells with a non-zero score. The default is -Inf.

only_pos

If TRUE, test only marker pairs whose median is higher in the level being tested than in the pooled remainder. The default is FALSE.

proximity_metric

The proximity metric to use. Any numeric column in the proximity score table can be selected. The default is "log2_ratio".

metric_type

One of "all", "self", or "co". "self" keeps pairs where both markers are the same protein, and "co" keeps pairs of different proteins.

p_adjust_method

One of "bonferroni", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "BH", "BY", or "fdr" (see ?p.adjust). P-values are adjusted within each one-versus-rest comparison.

verbose

Print messages.

Value

A tbl_df of test results stacked across comparisons.

Details

group_by must be a single column, for example "seurat_clusters" or "cell_type". For each level of that column, the level is compared to the remaining levels pooled into one reference group. Each comparison is delegated to DifferentialProximityAnalysis. With clusters 0, 1, and 2, the comparisons are 0 versus the pool of 1 and 2, 1 versus the pool of 0 and 2, and 2 versus the pool of 0 and 1.

The level being tested is stored in target. The pooled remainder is stored in reference and is labeled "rest", unless that label is already a level of group_by. A positive diff_median means the proximity metric is higher in target than in the pooled remainder. Set only_pos = TRUE to test only those pairs. Factor levels set the comparison order. Character labels are tested in order of first appearance. P-values are adjusted separately within each comparison, across the pairs that were tested.

Proximity scores are pivoted once with ProximityScoresToAssay. Each comparison then calls the matrix method of DifferentialProximityAnalysis on that same matrix. Missing scores are treated as 0.

A Seurat object created with load_proximity_scores = FALSE does not store proximity scores. Pass lazy = TRUE to fetch them with ProximityScores(object, lazy = TRUE).

See also

Other DA-methods: DifferentialProximityAnalysis(), RunDAA(), RunDCA(), RunDPA()

Examples

library(dplyr)
set.seed(1)
example_data <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  marker_1 = c("CD19", "CD3E"),
  marker_2 = c("CD19", "CD3E"),
  component = paste0("cell", seq_len(12))
) %>%
  mutate(
    join_count_z = rnorm(n()),
    seurat_clusters = dplyr::case_when(
      component %in% paste0("cell", 1:4) ~ "0",
      component %in% paste0("cell", 5:8) ~ "1",
      TRUE ~ "2"
    )
  )

# Compare each cluster with the cells in every other cluster
FindAllProximityMarkers(
  example_data,
  group_by = "seurat_clusters",
  proximity_metric = "join_count_z",
  min_cells_per_group = 4,
  verbose = FALSE
)
